Specification curve

Source: R/specrv.R
specrv.Rd

The estimate of a treatment effect under every reasonable specification at once, and whether the specifications as a whole show an effect: the specification curve of Simonsohn, Simmons and Nelson (2020). A finding that holds under one specification only is fragile; one that survives the choices an analyst could defensibly have made is not.

Usage

specrv(
  data,
  y,
  d,
  x = NULL,
  opt = NULL,
  se = c("hc1", "iid"),
  level = 0.95,
  null = c("perm", "boot"),
  nsim = 500,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'specrv'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit.

y

The names of the outcome columns (numbers): each is a specification of the outcome.

d

The name of the treatment column (numbers; it must vary).

x

NULL or the names of the covariates in every specification (numbers); for print(), an object of class specrv.

opt

NULL or the names of the optional covariates (numbers), at most ten.

se

"hc1" or "iid".

level

The level of the intervals and of significance: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

null

"perm" or "boot".

nsim

The data sets under the null: a whole number from 1 to 100000.

seed

NULL (drawn from R's generator, so set.seed() fixes it) or a whole number from 0 to 2147483647.

...

Not used by print().

Value

An object of class specrv, a list: spec, one row per specification (outcome, ctrl, the optional covariates in it or "none", est, se, stat, p, lo, hi, sig); test, one row per summary (stat: median, nsig, z; obs; p); sign, the dominant direction; dist, the summaries under the null (a matrix, NA for a draw left out); nok; and null, nsim, seed.

Details

The specifications are every outcome in y crossed with every subset of the optional covariates opt (2^length(opt) subsets, from none to all), the covariates x always in. Each is the least squares fit of the outcome on an intercept, the covariates and d, giving the coefficient of d with a classical or HC1 standard error and Student's t. The curve is summarised three ways (their sec. 3): the median estimate; the number of specifications significant at 1 - level in the dominant direction (the sign of the median); and the sum of the specifications' t statistics over the square root of their number. Each summary is compared with its values on nsim data sets where the null holds: with null = "perm" the treatment is permuted across rows (for a randomised treatment); with null = "boot" each specification's estimate is removed from its outcome (y - b d) and rows are drawn with replacement. The p-value of a summary is (1 + k) / (1 + nok), k of the nok usable data sets at least as extreme in the dominant direction; a bootstrap draw whose fit is singular is left out.

References

Simonsohn, U., Simmons, J. P. and Nelson, L. D. (2020). Specification curve analysis. Nature Human Behaviour, 4(11), 1208-1214. doi:10.1038/s41562-020-0912-z

Steegen, S., Tuerlinckx, F., Gelman, A. and Vanpaemel, W. (2016). Increasing transparency through a multiverse analysis. Perspectives on Psychological Science, 11(5), 702-712. doi:10.1177/1745691616658637

Examples

set.seed(7)
n <- 200
d <- data.frame(t = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5), age = runif(n, 18, 60),
                prior = rpois(n, 2), male = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5))
d$arrest <- 0.3 * d$t + 0.1 * d$prior + rnorm(n)
d$charge <- 0.2 * d$t + 0.1 * d$prior + rnorm(n)
s <- specrv(d, c("arrest", "charge"), "t", opt = c("age", "prior",
            "male"), nsim = 200, seed = 1)
s
#> specrv: 16 specifications, 0 significant; perm null, 200 data sets
#>    stat    obs       p
#>  median 0.1427 0.06468
#>    nsig 0.0000 1.00000
#>       z 3.9272 0.07463
head(s$spec)
#>   outcome        ctrl       est        se     stat          p          lo
#> 1  arrest        none 0.2145197 0.1434022 1.495931 0.13626394 -0.06827189
#> 2  arrest         age 0.2124390 0.1436782 1.478575 0.14085117 -0.07090585
#> 3  arrest       prior 0.2389817 0.1435041 1.665330 0.09743638 -0.04401974
#> 4  arrest age + prior 0.2373957 0.1437597 1.651337 0.10027101 -0.04611867
#> 5  arrest        male 0.2095342 0.1439181 1.455926 0.14700476 -0.07428369
#> 6  arrest  age + male 0.2077787 0.1442450 1.440457 0.15133357 -0.07669274
#>          hi   sig
#> 1 0.4973113 FALSE
#> 2 0.4957839 FALSE
#> 3 0.5219832 FALSE
#> 4 0.5209100 FALSE
#> 5 0.4933520 FALSE
#> 6 0.4922501 FALSE
